front.title: Autonomous Agent Identity and Runtime Control Status (AIID)

abstract.t:
Autonomous software agents increasingly take consequential actions on behalf of people and organizations. Existing identity systems (OAuth 2.0, SPIFFE, and the WIMSE workload identity architecture) authenticate such agents, but they do not define a common, vendor- neutral way for an accountable owner to place a running agent into a restricted state, nor a common way for a relying party to check that state immediately before acting.
This document defines AIID: a durable identifier for an autonomous agent, a small runtime control state machine (active, safe_mode, suspended, revoked), an asymmetric authority model in which automated monitors may only tighten state and only the accountable owner may loosen it, a namespace-wide freeze, and a pre-action status check with fail-closed semantics. AIID is designed to bind to, not replace, existing identity: it defines an "aiid" claim for OAuth 2.0 access tokens and corresponding token introspection members, bindings for SPIFFE and WIMSE identifiers, a mapping onto the OAuth Token Status List, and change notification using the OpenID Shared Signals Framework. It also defines compact signed action receipts, and an OPTIONAL enforcement gateway deployment profile.
